sources.title: Search the List – Find listed buildings, monuments, battlefields and more
sources.verified_claim: Historic England states the National Heritage List for England is the only official up-to-date register of nationally protected historic buildings and sites. Register authority does not establish that any sample parcel intersects an entry without an exact match.

sources.title: Download Listing Data - GIS Shapefiles
sources.verified_claim: Historic England's Open Data Hub publishes free GIS data and records listed-building polygons updated on 20 July 2026, with current designation datasets available in machine-readable formats. Fresh data availability is not the same as a completed candidate intersection.

sources.title: Search the Heritage at Risk Register
sources.verified_claim: Historic England provides a searchable and mapped 2025 Heritage at Risk Register. At-risk status applies to identified heritage assets and is not inferred for a candidate parcel without matching a registered asset.

sources.title: Annual Heritage at Risk Registers and Maps
sources.verified_claim: Historic England publishes annual versioned Heritage at Risk spreadsheets and maps and instructs users to use the relevant year. Version awareness prevents stale risk status being treated as current parcel evidence.

sources.title: Local Heritage Lists and Area Designations
sources.verified_claim: Historic England distinguishes local heritage lists and conservation areas from national statutory listing and explains their separate protection roles. The distinction is preserved and no candidate local designation is invented.

sources.title: Understanding List Entries
sources.verified_claim: Historic England explains that map markers may be for quick reference and that protected extents differ by designation type; full-scale maps and official entries may be needed. A map point is therefore not treated as exact legal extent.

sources.title: 2. Making best use of land and achieving Good Growth
sources.verified_claim: The 2026 Draft London Plan chapter includes Archaeological Priority Area and London-wide heritage mapping. Because the plan is draft, these maps are retained as emerging strategic evidence and not substituted for adopted or exact parcel constraints.

sources.title: Conservation Areas
sources.published_at: 2026 current dataset page; boundaries updated earlier
sources.verified_claim: The GLA dataset publishes conservation-area GIS boundaries but explicitly describes them as indicative and advises contacting the relevant borough to confirm accuracy. No exact candidate conservation-area intersection is asserted without borough confirmation and canonical spatial matching.
